title: deadline-aware token coalescer and predictive KV rewarm to smooth streaming tails
author: Marco Nguyen
release_notes: Introduce a deadline-driven token coalescer and a lightweight predictive KV rewarm path that reduces streaming tail latency (first-byte-to-next-byte variance) for small adaptive workloads. No API changes; opt-in via runtime flag 'stream.coalesce_deadlines=true'.
description: Motivation: Some production workloads show long, variable gaps between streamed tokens when model steps are short and requests interleave on the same worker. Previous fixes focused on credit pacing and jittered flushes; this PR targets the remaining tail variance by (1) coalescing emission of tokens from microbatches when close to application-level deadlines, and (2) opportunistically warming KV cache entries for likely-following sequences using a cheap predictor. Summary: Implement a "deadline-aware token coalescer" that groups tokens ready within a configurable deadline window (default 5ms) into a single write to the stream layer so small microbatch completions don't create many small writes. Add a predictive KV rewarm pass: when a request completes a token batch and sequence affinity heuristics indicate a follow-up is likely (short prompt, low perplexity hint), we prefetch the KV entries needed for the next few steps on the same model shard using a low-priority refill lane. Both features are disabled by default for strict determinism and can be enabled per-tenant or per-route. Implementation details: - runtime/streaming/coalescer.{cc,h}: new component sits between the token emitter and stream writer. Implements a deadline timer per-stream and drains tokens when either the deadline expires or the emitter reports a 'hard-ready' token. Uses high-resolution clock and avoids allocations on the hot path. - runtime/kv/predictive_rewarm.{cc,h}: lightweight predictor (n-gram-ish heuristic + token-length heuristic) that decides whether to issue a non-blocking KV prefetch for the next k steps. Prefetches use an opportunistic priority that never preempts active generation. - scheduler tweaks: changed schedule priorities to add a 'rewarm' lane; rewarm tasks are scheduled with deadline-insensitive background priority and bounded concurrency to avoid head-of-line interference. - configs: added stream.coalesce_deadlines (ms), stream.coalesce_max_batch, kv.rewarm.enabled, kv.rewarm.window_steps, kv.rewarm.max_concurrency. - unit + integration tests: coalescer unit tests for timing edge cases, integration test that simulates high interleaving between two streams and asserts improved inter-token variance. Commits: - 1a2f8b7: initial coalescer prototype + unit tests - 3b4d92e: integrate coalescer into emitter path, expose config - 6c8e41f: add predictive kv rewarm lane and scheduler integration - 9f1b33a: perf harness + benchmark results - eed2c4a: address reviewer comments, add safety caps and opt-out flags Files changed (high level): - runtime/streaming/coalescer.h (new) - runtime/streaming/coalescer.cc (new) - runtime/streaming/emitter.cc (touched) - runtime/kv/predictive_rewarm.h (new) - runtime/kv/predictive_rewarm.cc (new) - runtime/scheduler/scheduler.cc (touched) - runtime/config/defaults.yaml (touched) - test/streaming/coalescer_test.cc (new) - perf/bench/harness/stream_rewarm_bench.cc (new) Example snippet (coalescer): "if (now - first_ready_ts < cfg.coalesce_deadline_ms && batch.size() < cfg.coalesce_max_batch) { schedule_deadline_timer(stream_id, cfg.coalesce_deadline_ms - elapsed); return; } emit(batch);" Benchmarks: - Harnessed end-to-end with microbench workload that mimics short prompts + chat-like followups. Key numbers measured on rtx-a100 pool: - baseline median inter-token gap: 6.8ms, p95: 22.1ms - after coalescer only: median 5.1ms (-25%), p95 15.0ms (-32%) - after coalescer + predictive rewarm: median 3.9ms (-43%), p95 10.8ms (-51%) - cost impact: CPU overhead +0.6% on streamer nodes; KV prefetch bandwidth increase bounded to +3% under test traffic. Testing & CI: - Local unit tests added and passing. - CI: initial run showed a flaky streaming-integration test failure (timeout on unrelated backpressure test). Root cause: test timing assumptions invalidated by faster emissions; test updated to use condition-variable with elapsed threshold. Reran CI; all checks green (lint, unit, integration, performance smoke). Review conversation (highlights): - Ava: "Nice approach. Concerned about prefetch causing extraneous KV pressure on busy shards." - Marco: "Added bounded concurrency and heuristics: only prefetch when model shard idle < 40% and prefetch budget available; also per-tenant opt-out config." - Ravi: "Can we make the deadline window adaptive to observed inter-token variance?" - Marco: "Follow-up planned (ENG-2034) to add adaptive deadline tuning using moving quantiles; kept static default for safety in this PR." - Leah (approve): "Safety caps look good. Tests cover race cases I worried about." Merge notes: - Kept behavior behind flags and defaulted to off for tenants that require strict token-by-token determinism. - Squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Follow-ups / TODOs: - ENG-2034: adaptive deadline tuning based on moving quantiles and load signals. - Add telemetry: emit coalescer hit-rate, average coalesce-window, rewarm prefetch success rate, and prefetch miss ratio for further tuning. - Evaluate effectiveness on Dedicated customers with high interleaving (follow-up trials planned). Security/rollback considerations: - Prefetches are read-only and respect tenant isolation rules; no new persistent state persisted. - Fast rollback: set kv.rewarm.enabled=false and stream.coalesce_deadlines=0 to disable features at runtime without restart.
